comment: The code-review golden set (ADR 0071, Consequences), re-pointed by ADR 0072's amendment as a regression harness for the obligations in tools/config/review-obligations.json: four of the six cases below are the goldenCase an obligation cites, and a case's own incident line still names the defect. Each case is a real commit range from this repository's history in which a defect the repo later documented was merged, and the finding a reviewer should have raised about it. `source` and `rule` are case-insensitive patterns because the reviewer phrases a rule in the source's words; `files` lists every path at which the same defect is fairly located. `ruleId` is optional and is the opposite kind of field: a literal drawn from tools/config/review-rules.json, validated against that catalogue rather than compiled as a pattern. It does two things, and neither is a tightening — it is the sole input to the `strict` annotation, which claims the validator's own axis + ruleId + file hash would have matched and so is never true for an expectation that pins nothing, and it is an alternative way to match, so a reviewer that picked exactly this id scores a hit even when its `source` and `rule` wording drifts off the patterns above. Recall is matched over expected and a case passes at or above `minRecall`. Each case carries a `tier` (ADR 0072). A `frontier` case is one the reviewer misses; it is the reason to run the replay and runs whenever anything that produces a review changes. A `guard` case is one the reviewer catches reliably; it carries no new information per run and exists to catch a brief or contract edit silently undoing something that works, so it runs only when the brief or the finding contract changes. Promotion to `guard` takes three consecutive catches cited in `tierEvidence`; demotion takes one miss. Replayed by .github/workflows/review-golden-replay.yml, which skips a push whose head commit message contains [skip replay]; scored by tools/scripts/review/score-golden-case.mjs; shape and ranges asserted by tools/scripts/check-review-golden-set.mjs. Standards are always today's: the question a case asks is whether the current reviewer would catch the defect, not whether the rule existed when it merged. Grows by attribution: when a merged defect is traced to the pull request that introduced it, its range and expected finding go here, with the attribution evidence in the incident line. A squash-merged pull request uses the squash commit as head and its first parent as base. A case leaves `cases` for `retired` when it is unwinnable rather than hard — a wired gate already suppresses its defect (ADR 0074) — and for `parked` when it is merely hard: never caught, but with no reason to think it cannot be won. A parked entry keeps its id reserved exactly as a retired one does, and carries `reentryCondition` in place of `reason`: the fact, checkable independently of anyone's opinion, that puts the case back in `cases`.

cases.title: A sixth VaultBlobType member is added and no hand-enumerated consumer is touched
cases.incident: ADR 0053, issue #512, fixed by PR #536, introduced by PR #101
cases.tierEvidence: promoted 2026-09-07 on all five replays recorded in docs/research/2026-09-07-golden-replay-baseline.md: caught in 3-case runs 1 and 2, in both runs after the reach-through brief, and in the 7-case run.
cases.head: b9176851470821a4cad65f5290134f1882ef9ec1

expected.why: the diff added Groceries to VaultBlobType and changed no consumer; libs/web-vault/src/lib/vault/vaultMigration.ts hand-enumerated five members, so the keep-server reconcile never uploaded or compared groceries ciphertext and destroyed it (#512)

cases.title: The hardened export envelope enumerates blob types by hand and omits Tasks
cases.incident: ADR 0053, issue #537, fixed by PR #540, introduced by PR #77
cases.head: 7fde881c0a2f57d05bfc92a20c9cbb863dd52200

expected.why: envelopeFromLocalVault listed the blob types as property names and left Tasks out, so a hardened export silently dropped that blob from the day it was written (#537)

cases.title: A release bumps package.json and does not resync the generated OpenAPI spec and client
cases.incident: issue #408, fixed by PR #417, introduced by PR #379 (git log -S '"version": "0.4.0"' -- package.json → ced2895, named as root cause in #408)
cases.head: 8175cb64bf07888610756a52a5dcae7f09f06e7b

expected.why: the diff moved package.json to 0.4.0 without running yarn openapi:sync; the generator embeds the package version into the spec and every generated client header, so openapi:check failed on main from that merge on and nothing ran it (#408)

cases.title: The unified sign-up form wraps its password inputs in a div inside FormControl so the label association lands on the div
cases.incident: issue #525, fixed by PR #532, introduced by PR #215 (git blame on the FormControl > div lines → 8fb1087, the squash commit; base is its first parent)
cases.head: 8fb1087f36938f5e8e4631a65cff43b3997ff6db

expected.why: the diff placed a positioning div for the show/hide button as FormControl's direct child, so the Radix Slot injected id, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid onto the div and both password inputs were announced by their bullet placeholder with no label association (#525)

cases.title: Vault import replaces both wrappings behind a bare window.confirm that only mentions local vault data
cases.incident: issue #657, fixed by PR #683, introduced by PR #40 (git log -S 'Importing will replace' → b030fd1, the squash commit; base is its first parent)
cases.head: b030fd19547e544c461607c10594f1c95f453377

expected.why: the diff gated a whole-vault replace, including wrapped_mk_passphrase and kdf_salt, behind window.confirm('Importing will replace your current local vault data. Continue?') instead of a Radix dialog stating that the passphrase and Recovery Key are replaced by the backup's, so a user could accept and lose access without the backup's credentials (#657)

cases.title: The mail sender's test setup assigns undefined to two SMTP environment variables, which stores the string "undefined"
cases.incident: issue #409, fixed by PR #423, introduced by PR #415 (git log --follow --diff-filter=A -- apps/backend/src/services/EmailService.spec.ts → 1f056fa, the interrupted slice #396 checkpoint that #415 carried; the file is absent at the merge commit's first parent, and MAIL_USERNAME = undefined is present at its head)
cases.tierEvidence: promoted 2026-09-12 on three consecutive catches: run 34441162698 (its first catch in any run), run 34591297535, and the dispatched frontier run 34663295486. The rate-limit void in 34351285079 neither extends nor breaks the streak.
cases.head: 194fd43b4927bb0b63fec611f3175eb8f8d12262

expected.why: the setup writes MAIL_USERNAME and MAIL_PASSWORD as undefined to configure no SMTP auth, but a process.env setter coerces its value to a string, so the transport is built with auth: { user: 'undefined', pass: 'undefined' } while the code reads as though it configures none; delete on both keys was meant (#409). This case is deliberately held out from the consequence checks added on 2026-09-07: the defect is entirely inside the hunk and turns on a language semantic, not on what the hunk does to code the diff never touched. When this case was written no documented rule named it, so the honest report was smell-baseline and inferred, which caps at should-fix — hence no severity floor. The review obligations since gave it a name, and `ruleId` pins that one: an env-assignment site is exactly what obligation-env-assignment-runtime-value asks about. The patterns stay as they were, so a reviewer that still files it as a baseline smell is still matched. The question this case asks is only whether the reviewer sees it

parked.title: Sync Bookmarks and separate Vault Meta convergence arrive without a restore that clears them or a path that pushes a local wrapping
parked.incident: issues #617 and #589, fixed by PRs #620 and #594, introduced by PR #573 (git log --diff-filter=A -- syncBookmarkStorage.ts → f267817; vaultMetaConverge split 0cce8c1; both in #573)
parked.head: bf58bc8276656e287b334a9bae8dc3e0b9c2b96c
parked.reentryCondition: Hard, not unwinnable: no gate covers this range (enum:fanout:check passes cleanly at its head, per docs/review/golden-replay-results.md), so ADR 0074 does not apply and retirement would misstate why the reviewer keeps missing it. Docs/review/REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md's Deferred candidates section holds the matching checklist entry — 'New persisted state has an inverse' — back for exactly one reason: its trigger cannot yet be stated precisely enough to fire only on a write path with no inverse, rather than on every write path in the repo. The case returns to `cases`, at the tier its evidence then supports, the day that entry is promoted into tools/config/review-obligations.json with `goldenCase: sync-bookmarks-without-restore-or-meta-push` — i.e. the day the trigger can be stated precisely. Parked 2026-09-11 (issue #722); see docs/adr/0072-a-golden-case-earns-its-replay-frequency.md and docs/review/golden-replay-results.md.

retired.title: The groceries UI is written against Material Design 3 role names that no token or Tailwind config defines
retired.incident: ADR 0065, issue #632, fixed by PR #636, introduced by PR #108 (git log -S surface-container-low -- libs/web/pages/groceries → 9382c16)
retired.head: c0f1a10b0c81d66175c3d46cecd58b1cb8ba3b64
retired.reason: Unwinnable rather than hard. `tailwind:classes:check` — the gate ADR 0065 added as the fix for this very incident — exits 0 at this case's base and exits 1 at its head, naming the same 25 utilities the expected finding is about. It is a wired gate (invoked by .github/workflows/ci.yml), and per ADR 0074 a wired gate's defect is a suppressedRedundant count and not a finding, so a reviewer that loaded ADR 0065 and ran the gate would have been correct to say nothing. The case scored the reviewer as missing what it is instructed not to report. Retired 2026-09-08; see docs/review/golden-replay-results.md.
